CALDER SUPPLY CO. - INCIDENT REPORT IR-2026-031
Site: Groveport DC | Prepared by: Megan Strand, EHS Coordinator | Date prepared: 10/30/2026

Employee: Luis Ortega, Reach Truck Operator, 2nd shift (hire 08/29/2022). Supervisor: Keisha Wallace.
Date/time: Thu 10/29/2026, approx. 21:50. Location: Aisle 22, bay C, level 4.

What happened: Operator was lowering a pallet of cast iron fittings (2 SKUs, 46 cartons) from level 4. The top layer overhung the pallet by about 4 inches on the aisle side. When the mast tapped the front beam, the top carton slid. Operator reached outside the operator compartment with his left hand to stop it; the carton pinned his left wrist against the overhead guard. Load came down without further falls.

Witness: Terrell Vance (2nd shift lead) - saw the carton slide and the operator reach out; statement attached in the folder.

Property damage: rack upright 22-C-04 dented about 3 in. above base plate, aisle side. Bay unloaded and taped off 22:20. RT-14 inspected by Gary Hoffmann 10/30 06:30, no damage.

Operator training: PIT certification on file - initial 08/2022, last evaluation 03/12/2025 (reach truck), next evaluation due 03/2028.

items.subject: EHS-301 Injury and illness recordkeeping procedure (Rev. 3) - excerpt
items.body:
CALDER SUPPLY CO. - EHS-301 INJURY AND ILLNESS RECORDKEEPING (Rev. 3, 01/2025) - excerpt

1. Scope: all Calder employees and agency associates Calder supervises day to day (29 CFR 1904.31).
2. Reporting: every injury is reported to the supervisor the same shift. Nothing in our programs may discourage reporting (29 CFR 1904.35). No discipline for reporting an injury.
3. Facts: the Site EHS Coordinator collects the incident report, witness statements and all provider paperwork (work status and visit summary) and proposes a classification.
4. Determination: the Site Operations Manager makes the recordability determination. Questionable cases: consult the Director of EHS before the 7-day deadline.
5. Recording: recordable cases are entered on the OSHA 300 log and a Form 301 within 7 calendar days of receiving the information (29 CFR 1904.29(b)(3)).
6. Medical treatment vs first aid follows 29 CFR 1904.7(b)(5). Note: a prescription, or a provider's recommendation of an over-the-counter drug at prescription strength (for example ibuprofen over 467 mg per dose), is medical treatment.
7. Severe events: fatality to OSHA within 8 hours; in-patient hospitalization, amputation or loss of an eye within 24 hours (29 CFR 1904.39). Call the Director of EHS first.
8. Powered industrial trucks: after an operator is involved in an accident or near miss, refresher training and an evaluation are required before the operator returns to unrestricted truck duty (29 CFR 1910.178(l)(4)(ii)); document it in the PIT file.

items.subject: HR-210 Attendance (hourly associates, Distribution) - Rev. 2024
items.body:
CALDER SUPPLY CO. - HR-210 ATTENDANCE POLICY (hourly associates, Distribution), Rev. 03/2024

Points (rolling 12 months): tardy or early out under 2 hours = 0.5; absence (called in at least 1 hour before shift) = 1.0; no call / no show = 3.0.
Steps: 5.0 = verbal warning; 6.0 = written warning; 7.0 = final written warning; 8.0 = termination.
Not assessed (protected absences): FMLA-qualifying leave (own or a family member's serious health condition), absences related to an ADA accommodation, work-related injury or illness, jury duty, military leave, approved PTO, reasonable time to vote on election day (Ohio R.C. 3599.06), and bereavement under HR-215.
Before any termination under this policy the supervisor sends the points record to the HR Business Partner, who confirms that no assessed occurrence relates to a protected absence. Terminations need HR approval (FIN-104 Table C).
If an associate gives a reason that may be FMLA-qualifying (for example caring for a parent with a serious health condition), the supervisor tells HR within 2 business days. The associate does not have to say "FMLA".

Marcus,

What I'd do:
1. Move NBV-075FP to 14-D-01 so the sizes aren't next to each other. I found 9 other valve pairs in zone 14 with the same problem from the reset, I'd split those too.
2. Turn on item-scan confirm for zone 14 in Manhattan. It costs about 3% of pick rate in that zone.
3. Re-train the 10/19 agency class on item verification.

Andy
